baseline.name: Enumerate every unordered pair
baseline.approach: Test all i<j pairs for the target sum.
baseline.space: O(1) auxiliary, excluding the two-index output

archived.name: One-pass chained-hash lookup
archived.time: Expected O(n+B) with favorable hashing and O(n^2+B) worst case, where B=10007 buckets; fixed B gives the usual expected O(n) description
archived.space: O(n+B) auxiliary hash storage and a two-integer returned allocation

why: Looking up the complement reuses earlier work instead of checking every earlier value separately, provided hash chains stay short.
quantitative_comparison: The complete pair baseline visits n(n-1)/2 pairs. This source performs at most n outer iterations, but a lookup can traverse a long chain and success also scans B=10007 buckets for cleanup. Only expected growth improves under favorable hashing; there is no universal factor or measured time gain.
tradeoffs: Uses bucket/node allocations rather than constant auxiliary state. Collisions preserve a quadratic worst case, and unchecked allocations plus the invalid no-solution fallback limit robustness.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
